post.caption:
“I’ll start praying at 30.” You turn 30 on Friday. 🫒

Harvest day in your uncle’s olive grove. He points at the oldest row: “Your grandfather planted these. He was 30. He never tasted one — he died at 34.” He didn’t wait to be ready. He planted.

“Allah does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity.” (2:286)

This Maghrib: your first prayer. Don’t wait for 30.

captions: Sunday. Your uncle’s olive grove. Harvest day.
“At 30 I’ll be ready. Calmer. More serious.”
Your uncle points at the oldest row of trees.
“He never tasted one. He died at 34.”
His olives are in your hands now.
He didn’t wait to be ready. He planted.
That evening. A mosque courtyard you’ve walked past for years.
You forget the order of wudu. Nobody laughs.
Three rak’ahs of Maghrib. Clumsy. Real.
